name: Clay
look: Cream-tinted white with six saturated feature cards, generous radii and rounded display type at weight 500.

hero.title: Find the right people, with the right context
hero.sub: Enrich a list from fifty data providers in one pass, then write outreach that references something true rather than a merge field.

features.title: Fifty providers, one waterfall
features.sub: Ask for an email once and we try providers in order until one has it — you pay for the hit, not the attempt.

items.title: Waterfall enrichment
items.body: Providers tried in sequence until one returns a result. Coverage goes up and cost goes down.

items.title: Fifty sources
items.body: Contact, firmographic, technographic and intent data behind one interface and one bill.

items.title: Research agents
items.body: Ask a question about each row in plain language and get a researched answer, with the source.

items.title: Outreach that lands
items.body: Messages built from what you actually found rather than a first-name merge field.

items.title: Keeps itself current
items.body: Re-enrich on a schedule so the list does not quietly rot between campaigns.

items.title: Syncs both ways
items.body: Push to your CRM and read back what happened, so the list reflects reality.

showcases.title: Pay for the hit, not the attempt
showcases.body: A waterfall tries each provider in order and charges only when one returns data. Coverage typically lands well above any single vendor, at a fraction of holding contracts with all of them.

showcases.title: Research, not merge fields
showcases.body: An agent reads each company's site and answers your question per row — whether they run a particular stack, whether they are hiring, whether they just moved office. Outreach then references something real.
points: Runs on a schedule as the list changes

gallery.title: TEMPLATES
gallery.sub: Prospecting workflows people have already made work.

testimonial.quote: We cancelled three data contracts and got better coverage. The finance team asked me to explain it twice because it sounded wrong.
testimonial.name: Priya Nair

pricing.title: PRICING
pricing.sub: Credits for successful lookups. Nothing for misses.

items.a: One successful lookup that returned data. Failed attempts across the waterfall are not charged, which is the point of running providers in sequence.

items.q: Do I need contracts with the providers?
items.a: No. That is the value — one bill and one interface across fifty sources, without negotiating fifty agreements.
Providers are vetted for lawful basis and the source is recorded per field, so you can answer a subject access request without guessing.

items.q: Can I bring my own provider?
items.a: Yes, on Enterprise. Add an existing contract into the waterfall and use your own rates alongside ours.

cta.title: Enrich your first list
cta.sub: A hundred credits free, and you only pay for the rows that return data.

footer.tagline: Find the right people, with the right context.

notes: The canvas is cream-tinted white. That warmth is what separates it from every cool-grey competitor.
A six-colour saturated palette carries the feature cards — pink, teal, lavender, peach, ochre and cream.
3D claymation artefacts are the most recognisable visual element and belong at full bleed in the hero.
The display face is rounded at weight 500 with heavy negative tracking, which is what the generous radii are matching.
Radii step up deliberately: 12px buttons and inputs, 16px content cards, 24px feature cards.
